title: Inheritance and Alibi
premise: Bram Dravenmoor, a night-shift taxi dispatcher with an uncanny gift for reading the town's rhythms, has quietly untangled three deaths the police filed as accidents. When the coffin of beloved founder Edith Marlowe is exhumed and found empty, Bram is pulled in by a cryptic ledger hidden in the taxi company's old route books — a ledger that maps not streets but secrets. As the anniversary dinner approaches, she discovers Edith faked her death to escape blackmail by the founding families, who have been laundering the town's history into their fortunes. At the dinner, Bram exposes the conspiracy, choosing truth over the loyalty of the one friend who helped cover it up — and finally claims her own place in a town that never made room for her.
about_author: Jonah Whitlock spent a decade driving night cabs in small industrial towns before turning to crime fiction, collecting the stories passengers tell when they think no one is listening. He writes from a converted garage office, where he keeps every fare receipt he ever saved.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. During a slow night shift, Bram hears radio chatter about the exhumation of founder Edith Marlowe for a cemetery relocation — and learns the coffin came up empty. She drives to the graveyard on instinct, feeling the same pull that preceded her three unofficial investigations. Emotional beat: restless recognition that something is wrong beneath the town's polished surface.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, flashback-tinged. We learn how Bram solved three deaths the police dismissed: a mill foreman, a council clerk, a teenage runner. Each time she stayed silent, mailing anonymous tips. Now she wonders if those deaths connect to Marlowe. Emotional beat: guilt over the safety of anonymity versus the itch to step forward.

chapters.title: The Route Book
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Sorting the taxi company's archive for a records request, Bram finds Edith Marlowe's handwriting in a 1970s route book — fares logged to addresses that don't exist. The numbers repeat in patterns too regular for real customers. Emotional beat: the thrill of a puzzle that finally chooses her instead of the reverse.

chapters.title: Anniversary Preparations
chapters.summary: Deputy Mayor Corinne Hale's POV. The town prepares the 150th anniversary dinner honoring Marlowe's legacy. Corinne pressures police to close the empty-coffin question quietly before the celebration. Emotional beat: polished anxiety; the reader sees powerful people managing a story rather than seeking one.

chapters.title: A Fare to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. A late-night passenger asks to be taken to one of the phantom addresses from the route book — a lot where nothing stands. He leaves behind a matchbook from the Marlowe estate. When Bram returns, he's gone, and the dispatcher log shows his trip was paid in cash by someone at city hall. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Detective Okafor
chapters.summary: Detective Naomi Okafor's POV. Okafor, who quietly suspects Bram solved the three 'accidents,' confronts her with the pattern. Neither admits anything, but Okafor shares one detail: the exhumation order was signed twice, once after Marlowe's death and once last month. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two women who trust logic more than people.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram realizes the route book is a cipher: fare numbers correspond to dates, addresses to names of founding families, and totals to sums moved through the town's development fund. Edith wasn't dispatching cabs — she was tracking money. Emotional beat: awe at a dead woman's foresight, and fear of what the ledger implicates.

chapters.title: The Loyal Friend
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram confides in Marty, her oldest friend and the taxi company's mechanic, who reveals his father drove for Edith and vanished in 1974. Marty begs Bram to drop it — some truths cost the people left behind. Emotional beat: the first crack between belonging and truth; Bram promises nothing.

chapters.title: What the Mill Knew
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Reopening the foreman's death, Okafor finds he'd audited the development fund weeks before his fall. The file was flagged closed by someone still in office. Emotional beat: cold anger as institutional rot comes into focus, and the three accidents begin to look like maintenance.

chapters.title: Ghost Address
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following the cipher, Bram locates the phantom addresses' true point: a decommissioned substation where Edith kept documents. Inside, she finds Edith's confession letter — unfinished — and evidence she planned to disappear rather than die. Someone else has been there recently; cigarette ash is fresh. Emotional beat: vertigo — the dead woman is alive, and someone else is hunting her paper trail.

chapters.title: Corinne's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corinne's POV. Corinne discovers the route book is missing from the archive and realizes Bram has it. Torn between protecting her family name and cutting losses, she orders a quiet tail on Bram. Emotional beat: a villain with a conscience, drowning in inherited sin she didn't commit but profits from daily.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram spots the tail and uses her dispatcher skills to lose them through the night grid, then doubles back to photograph the substation documents. She mails copies to herself as insurance. Emotional beat: competence as armor, and loneliness — she can't tell anyone what she's carrying.

chapters.title: Marty's Father
chapters.summary: Marty's POV. Marty digs out his father's old duffel: a driver's uniform, a second route book, and a note reading 'If Edith calls, I'm already gone.' He understands now that his father helped Edith vanish and paid for it. Emotional beat: grief reframed; loyalty to the dead pulling against loyalty to the living friend.

chapters.title: The Second Signature
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor traces the recent exhumation signature to a retired judge tied to the founding families — someone wanted proof Edith was gone, or proof she wasn't. She warns Bram they're both visible now. Emotional beat: the investigation stops being private; the hunters know the hunted.

chapters.title: Break-In
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram's apartment is searched while she's on shift. Nothing obvious is taken, but her insurance envelope is gone — except Bram mailed decoys; the real copies sit in a cab's lockbox rotating through the fleet. Emotional beat: violation and defiance; the town has entered her home, so she stops playing defense.

chapters.title: Edith Alive
chapters.summary: Edith Marlowe's POV (revealed). In a lakeside cabin, the 96-year-old founder watches news of the exhumation, dictating corrections to her confession. She never intended the ledger to surface this way — but if it must, she'd rather it burn the guilty than protect her peace. Emotional beat: an old woman weighing survival against legacy, choosing fire.

chapters.title: Dinner Invitations
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram decodes the final cipher layer: the ledger's last entry is dated the night of the anniversary dinner, listing five family names and a sum marked 'settled.' Edith planned her disappearance for that very date decades ago — the anniversary is the key date everything orbits. Emotional beat: the trap's shape becomes visible, with the dinner as its jaw.

chapters.title: Offer
chapters.summary: Corinne's POV. Corinne privately offers Bram money and silence: walk away, and the past stays buried for everyone's sake, including Marty's father's memory. Bram refuses — not heroically, but tiredly, because she's done surviving other people's lies. Emotional beat: the price of survival named aloud and declined.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. At the dinner, Corinne unveils a memorial; Okafor arrests the retired judge on document fraud; Bram takes the stage during toasts and reads the ledger aloud, naming the fund's thefts across generations. Panic, denial, and one family patriarch lunging for the microphone. Emotional beat: cathartic rupture — the glass raised, then shattered.

chapters.title: Where Loyalty Lands
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. In the fallout, Marty admits he tipped off Corinne early on, terrified of losing Bram the way he lost his father. Their friendship survives, scarred. Edith's full confession clears the three 'accident' victims' names posthumously. Emotional beat: forgiveness without forgetting; truth's cost itemized and paid.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Cab
chapters.summary: Edith's POV. Edith, finally safe to be seen, rides a taxi through town at dawn — Bram driving, off-shift, off-duty. They talk like two survivors comparing scars. Edith asks why Bram kept solving deaths alone; Bram answers that she was waiting for a town worth telling. Emotional beat: quiet communion between keeper and keeper.

chapters.title: Dispatch
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, epilogue. Months later, Bram remains a dispatcher — but now also consults for Okafor, and the taxi company's archive is a public record. A new dispatcher trainee asks how she knew where to look. Bram says the town tells you everything; you just have to belong enough to listen. Final beat: belonging earned, not granted.
